use_when, avoid_when and consequences are general, honest and specific (new-construction/statement-still-changing/hypotheses-don't-line-up as avoid conditions; silent-gap failure mode as consequence). But the applicability.goal_shape field states the move applies to 'a covering/transfer theorem whose hypotheses are about a set A (non-empty, doubling |A+A| ≤ K|A|) and whose conclusion quantifies over a witness H (existence of a subspace with a size bound)' — that is the concrete math of this one instance, not the shape of the blueprint-node move, which is 'a lemma/theorem stated as a node with a frozen Lean name, whose proof is a chain of citations to already-stated upstream nodes declared in one \uses{} line'. As written it would wrongly imply the move is limited to covering/transfer theorems with a doubling hypothesis. Fix: rewrite goal_shape to the general goal class and drop (or clearly mark as this instance) the covering/transfer/doubling/subspace content.
